articles.title: Jordan Chiles announces comeback bid for third Olympics at LA 2028
articles.summary: Olympic champion targets third Games in LA. Michael Jordan narrates announcement video. Chiles joins Lee and Carey on comeback trail. Jordan Chiles is returning for a run at her third Olympics, ⁠announcing Wednesday she intends to compete in the 2028 Games in Los Angeles.
body: Chiles shared ⁠her decision ⁠in ​a video narrated by basketball legend Michael Jordan.
Chiles, 25, owns a 2024 gold medal ‌from Paris and a 2021 silver from Tokyo in team competitions.

She won an individual bronze in 2024 on floor exercise before the medal was taken away by the Court of Arbitration for Sport and ‌given to Romania’s Ana Barbosu after a score inquiry. Chiles appealed the decision to the ​CAS and awaits a ruling.
Chiles starred at UCLA and won two NCAA titles in floor exercise (2023, 2026) and two others on bars (2023, 2025). She is a 23-time ⁠All-American who recorded 19 perfect-10s.

articles.title: Boulter wins one game in 58-minute US Open defeat
articles.summary: British number one Katie Boulter is dumped out in the second round of the US Open as she wins just one game in a 58-minute demolition by Karolina Muchova.
body: British number one Katie Boulter endured a "bad day at the office" as she won just one game in a 58-minute demolition by Wimbledon runner-up Karolina Muchova in the US Open second round.
The match, originally scheduled to be played on one of the outer courts, was moved to the 14,000-capacity Louis Armstrong Stadium after heavy rain in New York.

But fans who had counted themselves lucky to have gained a third match on their day session ticket may have been left feeling short-changed, as Boulter fell to a swift 6-1 6-0 defeat by the Czech seventh seed.
"Ultimately, it was a bad day at the office – times two," said Boulter.

articles.summary: Australia’s No 1 beats Andrea Guerrieri 6-2, 6-2, 6-4 after delays. Taylah Preston and Daria Kasatkina bow out after first-round defeats. After having his tournament opener against Andrea Guerrieri postponed until day four, Alex de Minaur had to endure another two-hour rain delay before putting…
body: The world No 7 advanced with a 6-2, 6-2, 6-4 victory to set up a second-round clash with Dutchman Botic van de Zandschulp.
In a clinical display, De Minaur broke Guerrieri twice in all three sets and only dropped serve once, when he was trying to close out the match at 5-2 in the third.
But New York’s miserable weather has left De Minaur facing a scheduling backlog and needing to win seven best-of-five-set matches in 12 days to lift the trophy.
“These tournaments, it’s all about adapting and that’s the name of the game,” he said.

articles.title: Championship roundup: Wrexham rout Millwall to seal first league victory
articles.summary: Kieffer Moore and Jacques Ekomié score in 3-0 win. QPR beat Cardiff; Middlesbrough draw at Burnley. Wrexham powered to their first Championship win this season with a ruthless 3-0 rout of injury-plagued Millwall on Wednesday.
body: The Welsh side had drawn with Cardiff and Watford before losing at home to Birmingham prior to this match. But they bounced back in emphatic fashion in south London to kickstart their bid for promotion to the Premier League after narrowly missing out on the playoffs last term.

The Millwall defender Zak Sturge deflected Issa Kaboré’s cross into his own net for a first-half own goal. Wrexham’s striker Kieffer Moore lashed in the second from 20 yards soon after half-time and Jacques Ekomié wrapped up the victory with a close-range finish.

After starting with two clean sheets in victories over Bristol City and Norwich, it is now eight goals conceded in two games for Millwall, who were thrashed 5-1 by Southampton on Saturday. Millwall lost their striker Josh Coburn and midfielder Casper De Norre to injuries during the game as their fitness woes mounted 24 hours after Nigeria winger Femi Azeez joined Brighton for £15m.
Rumarn Burrell scored both goals as QPR beat Cardiff 2-1 at Loftus Road to extend their impressive start to the season.

articles.title: Man City buy costly new midfield - but have they overlooked Haaland cover?
articles.summary: Manchester City have completed a squad overhaul including a fully revamped midfield to the tune of a Premier League record £458m, but that eyewatering number does not tell the full story.
body: Manchester City have completed their squad overhaul - including a fully revamped midfield - to the tune of £458m, a new Premier League record for a summer window.

New Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca received the full backing of director of football Hugo Viana in his first transfer window in charge after replacing Pep Guardiola. Indeed, City's record transfer fee was twice broken this summer.

A joint-British record £125m was spent on Maresca's former Chelsea skipper Enzo Fernandez after £116m was committed on Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest. Morocco international Ayyoub Bouaddi, 18, was also brought in for £86m. The trio accounted for the bulk of City's summer incomings.
The departures of captain Bernardo Silva, 2024 Ballon d'Or winner Rodri, Tijjani Reijnders and Nico Gonzalez means the City midfield has been completely transformed.

articles.title: Clippers Send Angry Letter To Adam Silver After Shocking Ruling
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Clippers finally got an answer on the NBA's cap circumvention investigation, but it's not the one they were hoping for. Despite claiming innocence and complying with the league throughout the process, NBA Commissioner Adam Silver came down with strict penalties, including a $30…
body: Instead of accepting their losses, however, the Clippers plan to fight with everything they have. After making their initial statement today, they shared their official email to the Commissioner, in which they called him out on the way this investigation was conducted. According to the Clippers, they worked tirelessly to comply with the league office, committing millions of dollars and many hours to prove their innocence.

“Unfortunately, none of those promises have been kept. In the last year, Steve Ballmer has spent nearly $50 million funding an investigation by Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz that has stretched far beyond the bounds of what the league set out to investigate, let alone the bounds of ‘fundamental fairness.’ The Clippers have produced more than 30,000 documents and provided more than 20 witnesses who have sat for 30 interviews.”

articles.summary: An interruption from a pair of birds ruffles Daniil Medvedev's feathers but fails to disrupt the seventh seed as he eases into the US Open third round with a dominant victory over Sebastian Gorzny.
body: The two birds settled down on the net for a closer look at the action midway through a second-set rally, with play continuing around them for several strokes before the chair umpire called for the point to be replayed.

Medvedev, who placed the incident in his "top five" most unusual experiences at the New York major, was visibly stunned by the decision which came just after he thought he had won the point with a cross-court forehand.
"This is very bad," the 2021 champion said as he remonstrated at the umpire on court.

Russia's Medvedev is no stranger to losing his composure on court, notably receiving a fine of almost £31,500 at last year's US Open for an extraordinary meltdown during his first-round defeat to Benjamin Bonzi.

articles.title: CEO and President of Good Good no longer with company after weekslong ad scandal
articles.summary: It appears that the Good Good Golf saga is circling towards a conclusion. On Wednesday, a report from Lucia Moses at Business Insider revealed an internal memo that was shared to Good Good employees which noted that co-founder and CEO Matt Kendrick “decided to step down,” and relatively new Good…
body: For those who have been blessedly, relatively unaware of this story until now, a quick recap. Good Good Golf is a YouTube channel turned all-around golf brand that was one of the biggest success stories in the sport’s social media space. Good Good had partnerships across golf brands, sold plenty of merch, and had even was set to sponsor a PGA Tour this fall.

Two weeks ago, an ad produced by Good Good for a new driver cobranded with Callaway was released over Callaway’s social channels. That ad depicted Garrett Clark, one of the founders of Good Good, tackling a woman who dared to touch his driver. The reaction to the ad was immediate and obvious, as none of the brands working alongside Good Good wanted to be associated with violence against women in defense of a golf club. Callaway quickly pulled the ad.

An initial apology missed the mark, and crucially, did not break down just where in the chain of command things fell apart to allow such a bad idea to go public. From there, more apologies followed. Clark posted an eight-minute long front-facing video apology to social media explaining that the ad was meant to be a parody of the film Obsession.

articles.title: Vlad Drives In 5, Jays Beat Guardians
articles.summary: Jays 11 Guardians 0. Let’s start by saying that Dylan Cease was excellent tonight. Four hits, no runs against, no walks and four strikeouts. He came out after six innings and 83 pitches because we need him for the rest of the month.
body: One in the first: Brett Bateman singled to start the game. And, an out later, Vladimir Guerrero doubled him home (a sign of things to come).

Five in the second: With one out, Ernie Clement singled (nice to see, he's had a tough time of it lately). Ernie stole second. Then Andrés Giménez singled him to third. Myles Straw walked to load the bases. Bateman hit into a 3-2 force at the plate. George Springer hit a soft grounder to short, that SS Angel Genao fielded and then threw 5-10 feet over the head of the second baseman. That scored two more. And Vlad homered, 3 more RBI.

One in the third: With one out, Nathan Lukes singled. Clement hit one to third; they got the runner at second and threw to first. The call on the field was out, but it was overturned on a Jays Challenge. It was very close; I didn't think they would make the change. Giménez singled. And Straw doubled, bringing in a run. 7-0.
Two in the sixth: With one out, Straw singled, Bateman walked, and Springer doubled. 8-0. And Vlad singled, 9-0.

Four hits, no runs against, no walks and four strikeouts.

articles.title: Angels’ Outfield Depth in Trouble After Josh Lowe Injury Scratch
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Angels scratched outfielder Josh Lowe from Wednesday’s game against the New York Yankees with neck stiffness. The Angels’ outfield is severely lacking in depth, as they currently have just four outfielders listed on their active roster—one of whom is Lowe.
body: Lowe, an offseason acquisition from the Tampa Bay Rays, has been with the Angels for nearly the entire season, only being away from the team during a month-long stint in Triple-A. He can play any position across the outfield, providing valuable depth in each position for the Halos.

The 28-year-old has 10 homers on the year, driving in 27 runs through 95 games this season. He has a.625 OPS this season, which would be the lowest mark of his career if he finishes the season at this pace.

His best stretch of baseball came after the Angels recalled him from Triple-A in June, where he went 8-for-18 through his final six games of June. He hit a homer and drove in four runs during that stretch, posting an OPS north of 1.000 during his hot streak.
Siri, Meckler and Mike Trout are the only other players explicitly listed as outfielders on the Angels’ roster, though they have other players who could stand in if needed.

articles.title: Boulter crushed by Muchova but Jones joins Dart in second round at US Open
articles.summary: Katie Boulter suffered a nightmare US Open exit in a punishing straight sets defeat to Karolina Muchova in under an hour at Flushing Meadows.
body: The British No 1 was broken in all seven of her service games in a chastening 6-1 6-0 defeat inside 58 minutes on Louis Armstrong Stadium.
Boulter traded breaks with Muchova at the start of the first set only for the 2026 Wimbledon finalist to pull clear and put on a clinic for her beleaguered opponent.
Boulter double faulted eight times and produced 22 unforced errors in a nightmare, error-strewn performance that left her hopes of progressing in tatters.
"Ultimately, it was a bad day at the office - times two," said Boulter. "I struggled with the conditions. I struggled with the roof, the noise, I let things distract me.
